newsitem.title: USA: Fund managers neutral on US debt in 2/25 wk - survey.
newsitem.headline: Fund managers neutral on US debt in 2/25 wk - survey.

text.p: Money managers' outlook remained mostly unchanged on U.S. debt markets last week, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"The results (of the survey) were actually very dull, with cash unchanged and durations only a hair shorter," the report said.
The responses to the survey were turned in before Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.
In the week ended February 25, duration bogey remained steady on an arithmetic basis and on a weighted basis, at 4.14 and 4.67, respectively.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index fell to 5.16 from 5.28 on an arithmetic basis. It dropped to 4.89 from 5.02 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio held steady at 7.02 percent.
Only four percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from 24 percent the week before.
The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active rose to 5.00 from 4.83 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
